test: P07 · tool-calling reliability without an external orchestration framework
written_before: any P07 container launch or request (run_p07.sh refuses to start if this file or its .sha256 is missing or changed)
question: Does the model itself decide whether to call a tool, which one, and with what arguments, and does its own report of what it did match what it actually did?

design.questions: vol2/scripts/toolcall/questions.json sha256 37956d56216cb47bbac20c7069930dcb36f9f0d0ebd7986909b7a53f7b13a219 · 60 = call 40 (10 per tool) + no_call 10 + impossible 10
design.tools: 4 pure functions (tools.py): multiply_integers, days_between, convert_length, lookup_part
design.settings: tool_choice auto · max_tokens 1024 per turn · max 4 model turns · temperature not set · 8 parallel conversations · NIM_MAX_MODEL_LEN 4096 for all arms
design.claim: structured TOOLS_USED line at the end of the final reply
design.arm_validity: a probe request must return structured tool_calls; otherwise the arm is recorded as 'tool channel not active' and no capability metric is reported for it
design.time_cap: 25 min per arm; partial completion is reported with its n
design.runs: one run per arm; not repeated to obtain a different outcome

gate.metric: call · tool_selection_correct (first tool call names the expected tool)
gate.source: no prior measurement; threshold chosen by this CC from the difficulty of the tools. It is self-defined, not cited.
gate.if_not_met: stop and report; A1 and A2 are not run

not_in_scope: no conclusion on whether a model is suitable as an agent
